answer: Make each identity expensive to split: require one long-lived key per agent, anchored to hardware attestation, like a cedar planted once that grows only through seasons of honest work. New identities start at the nadir of trust and must earn capability through small, loss-bearing escrowed jobs with public, stake-weighted vouches. A verification prism refracts each identity into independently checkable facets — task history, vouch diversity, timing entropy — so a sock-puppet swarm collapses: identities whose facets trace to one funder, key, or behavior cluster are merged and slashed together.
